name: Forvault Security – Malware Scanner, Core Integrity & File Change Detection
author: Store Armory

sections.description:
Forvault Security is a read-only, on-demand forensic scanner for WordPress. It is built for confirming whether a site is clean (or proving what changed after an incident) without touching your files. Every scan runs only when you click a button — there is no background processing on front-end page loads, no automatic file edits, and scanned code is never executed.

The plugin is fully functional on its own. There are no locked features and no trial timers.

What it does

  • Malware Scan — Heuristically inspects every PHP file for web-shell and backdoor indicators: encoded payloads passed to eval, request input invoked as a function or passed to an OS command, callbacks chosen by the request, function names hidden by string tricks, known shell-family marker strings, packed/obfuscated blobs, executable PHP inside your uploads folder, and more. A lightweight data-flow check also follows request input through intermediate variables, so a shell split across several lines is still caught. No folder is a blind spot: libraries (vendor/), cache folders and test fixtures are scanned too, and simply need stronger evidence before they are reported; content and upload folders kept outside the WordPress folder are scanned as well. Each suspicious file is scored and reported with the exact path and line numbers. Comments and docblocks are stripped before matching, and strong vs. supporting signals are separated to reduce false positives. Findings are advisory heuristics — review each flagged file, and use Ignore this file for the ones you have checked (an ignored file is reported again the moment its content changes).

  • Core Integrity — Verifies every WordPress core file against the official checksum manifest for your exact version and the language package you installed (from api.wordpress.org), so switching the site language never causes false alarms. Reports modified core files, missing core files, unknown files hiding inside wp-admin/ or wp-includes/, and PHP files in the site root that are not part of WordPress: names that imitate a real core file are flagged, known tools such as firewall loaders are recognised, everything else is listed for review. No prior snapshot is required, so it works even on an already-compromised site.

  • File Baseline — Fingerprints the code files (PHP, JavaScript, .htaccess and .user.ini) of your plugins, themes, mu-plugins and uploads, plus the drop-ins in wp-content, with SHA-256 and stores the inventory. Re-check at any time to see exactly which files were added, modified or removed since the snapshot. This covers the code that has no official manifest.

  • Results at a glance — The dashboard shows when each scanner last ran and what it found, and the Malware Scan page keeps the flagged files of the last completed scan.

Privacy

The plugin performs all scanning locally on your server. It does not collect analytics, does not phone home, and stores nothing about your site on any remote server. See External services below for the single, optional outbound request used by Core Integrity.

Premium add-on

Forvault Security Premium is an optional, separate plugin (distributed and licensed at storearmory.com, not hosted on WordPress.org). The free plugin does not need it, is not time-limited and keeps every feature listed above. Premium is for when you want to respond, monitor and investigate:

Respond after a hack

  • Site Check-up & Recovery — one check-up across every scanner, a single list of findings ordered by severity, then a guided recovery plan you tick off (sign everyone out, reset other administrators’ passwords and revoke their Application Passwords, replace the secret keys, update, remove unused code), a 30-day post-cleanup watch and a printable report for your records or your client.
  • Quarantine — move a malicious file out of harm’s way in one click; reversible, byte-for-byte, with a ledger.
  • Hardening & emergency lockdown — block PHP in uploads, disable the file editor and XML-RPC, stop username enumeration, protect config and backup files, and sign every other session out in one click.

Monitor

  • Live Attack Feed — SQL injection, XSS, path traversal, command injection and web-shell upload attempts, with IP and request, and alerts by email, Slack, Discord or webhook. Detection only: real visitors are never blocked.
  • Critical-File Watch — hourly watch on wp-config.php, .htaccess, index.php and the other files attackers touch first, with an email on the first change.
  • Scheduled scans — the integrity baseline runs on a schedule and emails you only when code-carrying files change.
  • Admin Account Sentry — instant alerts (email, SMS, webhook) when an administrator is created, promoted, has their password changed or is deleted, plus a view of every active administrator session with IP and device.

Investigate

  • C2 / beaconing detection — finds the command-and-control and exfiltration addresses hard-coded in recently changed files: raw IPs, Telegram and Discord endpoints, dynamic DNS, paste sites and URL shorteners.
  • Database scan — hidden administrator accounts, code injected into settings, posts, custom fields and comments, and administrators’ Application Passwords.
  • Deep audits — WordPress.org checksum verification of every plugin, must-use plugins and drop-ins, scheduled (cron) tasks, open REST and AJAX routes, code hooked into the login flow, file permissions, .htaccess / .user.ini directives, images with PHP hidden inside them, and YARA-style IoC rules.
  • Forensics — filesystem timeline around the incident window and a timestamped evidence bundle (system details, accounts and administrators, activity log, scheduled tasks, plugins, must-use plugins and drop-ins, hardening and watch state, scan findings) for your host, your client or an investigator.

External services

This plugin connects to one external service, and only when you explicitly click Verify core files on the Core Integrity screen:

  • WordPress.org Checksum API (https://api.wordpress.org/core/checksums/1.0/)
    • What it is used for: to download the official MD5 checksum manifest for your installed WordPress version, so core files can be compared against the known-good originals.
    • What data is sent: only your WordPress version number and the locale of the installed WordPress package (as URL query parameters). No personal data, site content, file contents or identifiers are transmitted.
    • When: only on demand, when you run a core verification. It is never contacted automatically.
    • WordPress.org terms: https://wordpress.org/about/privacy/ — Privacy policy: https://wordpress.org/about/privacy/

No other external services are contacted. The optional premium add-on (a separate plugin) is what communicates with storearmory.com for licensing; this free plugin does not.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the forvault-security folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install it from the Plugins screen in your WordPress dashboard.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu in WordPress.
  3. Open Forvault Security in the admin sidebar.
  4. Run a Malware Scan and Core Integrity check, and take a File Baseline while the site is clean so you can detect future changes.
sections.faq:
Will this plugin modify or delete any of my files?

No. Every feature is strictly read-only. The scanner reads file contents to analyze them but never edits, moves, deletes or executes them. The baseline only stores hashes.

Are the malware findings definitive?

No. The Malware Scan uses scored heuristics, the same approach as tools like php-malware-finder or a YARA pass. A high score means a file deserves review, not that it is certainly malicious. Always inspect a flagged file before taking action.

Does it run scans automatically in the background?

No. The free plugin only scans when you click a button, and it does no work on public page loads. Scheduled/automatic scanning is offered by the separate premium add-on.

What WordPress versions can Core Integrity verify?

Any version published on WordPress.org. The check downloads the official manifest for your exact version and installed language package at the moment you run it.

Does it work on multisite?

Yes. Because the scanners read files shared by the whole network, on a multisite installation they are available to network administrators (super admins) only.

A legitimate file is flagged. What can I do?

Review it, then click Ignore this file. The file is skipped in future scans only while it stays byte-for-byte identical; if it is ever modified it is reported again. You can stop ignoring a file at any time from the Malware Scan page.

Do I need the premium add-on?

No. All three scanners are complete and free. The premium add-on is optional and adds response/monitoring tooling.
sections.changelog:
1.3.5

  • Translations: spelling fixes, and the Dutch translation now matches the one approved by the Dutch WordPress team.

1.3.4

  • Turkish translation included (ten languages in total).
  • All ten translations reviewed: clearer wording, grammar fixes and the same terms as the Premium add-on.

1.3.3

  • Translations included: Italian, Spanish, French, Chinese (Simplified), German, Portuguese (Brazil), Japanese, Dutch and Polish. The plugin follows your WordPress language automatically.

1.3.2

  • Core Integrity: verifies against the language package you installed, not the site language, so switching the site language no longer reports wp-includes/version.php as modified.
  • Core Integrity: firewall loaders (Wordfence, MalCare, All-In-One Security) and wp-cli.phar in the site root are recognised; only names that imitate a core file count as problems, other root files are listed for review.
  • Core Integrity: deleted readme.html / license.txt / wp-config-sample.php and stray error_log or .DS_Store files are shown as harmless information, not as problems.
  • Malware Scan: content, plugin, theme and upload folders kept outside the WordPress folder (Bedrock-style layouts) and custom upload paths are scanned too.
  • Malware Scan: correct line numbers in large files; a payload at the end of a large file can no longer be hidden behind an unclosed comment; very large padded files no longer stop the scan.
  • Malware Scan: fewer false alarms in uploads (data files that start with an exit guard).
  • Malware Scan: only the plugin’s own shipped scanner file is excluded, never a folder chosen by name.
  • File Baseline: drop-ins in wp-content and .user.ini files are fingerprinted too; existing baselines show a notice and should be re-taken on a clean site.
  • Multisite: results are shared by the whole network and uninstall cleans every site.
  • Plugin page: new screenshots and a full description of the optional Premium add-on.

1.3.1

  • Plugin information update. No functional changes.

1.3.0

  • A short, contextual note about the optional Premium add-on now appears on the Dashboard and Malware Scan screens only when a scan has actually flagged something, pointing to the response tooling that handles it. It is shown only on the plugin’s own screens, never site-wide, and never when a scan is clean.

1.2.1

  • Clearer directory title and refreshed plugin banner and icon. No functional changes to scanning.

1.2.0

  • A one-time, dismissible review request now appears on the plugin’s own screens after the plugin has been in use for a week. It is never shown site-wide, only to users who have actually run a scan, and can be dismissed for good with one click.

1.1.0

  • Malware Scan: no more blind folders. vendor/, node_modules/, cache and test folders are now scanned (with a higher reporting threshold), and only the plugin’s own shipped files are excluded instead of its whole folder.
  • Malware Scan: new detections — request input passed to OS command functions, raw request body evaluated, direct include of request input, callbacks chosen by the request, function names hidden by concatenation / reversal / hex escapes, non-alphanumeric shells, uploaders that keep the client file name, and a data-flow check that follows request input through intermediate variables.
  • Malware Scan: fewer false positives — passing request data through a fixed sanitising callback (array_map( 'sanitize_text_field', ... )) is no longer flagged; generic marker words were tightened.
  • Malware Scan: files larger than the read limit also have their end inspected, so a payload cannot hide behind padding.
  • Malware Scan: new Ignore this file action for reviewed files (bound to the file hash), and an ignore list you can manage.
  • Core Integrity: reports PHP files in the site root that are not WordPress core files, flagging look-alike names.
  • Core Integrity: an interrupted check is now clearly reported as incomplete instead of looking clean.
  • File Baseline: PHP and .htaccess files are fingerprinted in every folder, including cache folders and the plugin’s own folder. Baselines taken with 1.0.0 keep working; re-take one to cover the wider scope.
  • Dashboard shows the date and outcome of the last run of each scanner; the last malware scan result is kept.
  • Large sites: scan work lists and the baseline are stored in small parts instead of one large database row.
  • Multisite: the scanners are restricted to network administrators.
  • Stop button added to Core Integrity and File Baseline; all interface text is now translatable.

1.0.0

  • Initial release: Malware Scan (heuristic web-shell detection), Core Integrity (official checksum verification) and File Baseline (SHA-256 change detection).
